questions.q: What is the central argument this chapter makes about identity in a hybrid/multi-cloud architecture?
options: Identity is the layer that makes the architecture one coherent system, because every other pattern assumes a consistent answer to who's allowed to do this
Identity is a minor housekeeping detail that can be solved after networking and data architecture are finished
Each cloud environment should keep identity fully separate for better security isolation
Identity only matters for human users, not for architectural decisions like networking or governance
questions.explain: The chapter's throughline is that hybrid sync, SAML federation, and extended Conditional Access aren't three separate projects — together they form one identity plane that every later architectural decision depends on being solid.

questions.q: What is an "offboarding gap," as described in this lesson?
options: A delay in issuing a new employee's first laptop
A missing field in an HR onboarding form
A scheduling conflict in a live training session
The security hole left when an account is disabled in one directory (like on-prem AD) while an un-federated copy elsewhere, like a standalone AWS IAM user, keeps working
questions.explain: An offboarding gap happens when disabling someone in one identity store doesn't propagate everywhere — exactly the risk federation closes by making AWS consume the same identity instead of keeping its own.

questions.q: Why do federated AWS sign-ins improve audit correlation compared to standalone IAM users?
options: Federated sign-ins to AWS IAM Identity Center appear in Entra ID's sign-in logs alongside every other app that user touched, making it easy to match activity back to one real identity
AWS CloudTrail is disabled entirely once federation is configured
Standalone IAM users generate more detailed logs than federated sign-ins
Audit correlation is unrelated to whether a sign-in was federated or not
questions.explain: A federated sign-in shows up in Entra ID's sign-in logs under a real identity, unlike an unfederated IAM user visible only in AWS CloudTrail under a username an auditor has to manually match back to a person.

questions.q: How does Privileged Identity Management (PIM) extend to AWS once access is governed by federated groups?
options: PIM can only govern Azure resources and has no relationship to AWS whatsoever
PIM automatically deletes AWS accounts that go unused for 90 days
PIM governs eligibility for the group that grants an AWS admin-level permission set, making that access just-in-time instead of a standing permission
PIM replaces Conditional Access entirely for AWS sign-ins
questions.explain: Because AWS admin access is reachable through a federated group, PIM can govern eligibility for that group the same way it governs an Azure Owner role — turning standing admin access into time-boxed, approved elevation.

questions.q: Why does this chapter argue identity has to be solved before networking, data architecture, or governance across clouds?
options: Because networking and data architecture are always easier problems than identity
Because every later pattern assumes a consistent, already-solved answer to who's allowed to access a given resource across environments
Because AWS and Azure networking cannot technically function without Entra ID
Because governance tooling requires identity to be configured first for licensing reasons only
questions.explain: A shared network path or data layer doesn't mean much if the identity behind every request to use it is still three disconnected stories — identity is the foundation the rest of the course's patterns build on.
